description: How a hypoxic/anoxic brain injury can happen during labor, and why fetal monitoring strips become vital evidence when there is birth malpractice.
shortAnswer: If your infant suffers a reduced oxygen supply to the brain (cerebral hypoxia) or complete oxygen deprivation (cerebral anoxia) a hypoxic/anoxic brain injury could be the tragic result. It is imperative that mom and baby are continually monitored during active labor. If proper monitoring is not performed and your baby is injured, you may have a medical negligence case.

faq.q: What is fetal monitoring during labor used for?
faq.a: Fetal Monitoring during labor is commonly performed in all hospitals and is in part used to detect hypoxia during labor that could cause your baby to suffer a brain injury.

faq.q: Why do fetal monitoring strips matter in a birth injury case?
faq.a: When there is birth malpractice and your baby has a brain injury the fetal monitoring strips become vital evidence. They can help your attorney pinpoint when your baby went into distress and establish what steps the nurse or doctor responsible for your baby's care should have taken to address the problem.
